solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Final Indie and FT vie for circulation

indicators.note: newspapers put out for circulation are sent around and mixed about, so these letters get reshuffled

explanation.surface: Two newspapers squabble over readership figures to settle who comes out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for circulation' rearranges INDIE, FT and VIE together; the newspaper talk makes circulation look like sales figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a definitive version or verdict is the conclusive, last-word one.

clue.text: Sublime joke not good for charming?

indicators.note: with 'not good', this says the G is dropped and the joke word stands in its place

parts.note: magic, as an adjective, means enchanting or charming
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: Asks whether a lofty performance comes from a weak gag rather than real charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good for' means take G out of MAGIC and put JEST where it was: MA + JEST + IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something majestic is grand and stately, which is what sublime means.

clue.text: Several countries collectively deploy force in republic, ignoring cost

indicators.note: the force letter is deployed inside what remains of the republic
ignoring the word cost means it is left out of the republic's name

parts.note: Costa Rica is a Central American republic
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: A bloc of nations sends troops into a republic regardless of the expense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Several countries collectively' is a continent. Costa Rica is the Central American republic; dropping the word 'cost' leaves the rest, and 'in' takes the force letter inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A continent is made up of many nations, so the name stands for a whole group of countries.

clue.text: In Troon, take out good new driver by all means

indicators.note: take out means remove these letters from the venue

parts.note: Royal Troon in Scotland is a famous links where the Open is played
a learner driver displays an L plate

explanation.surface: A golfer at Troon is told to remove a decent new club from the bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' looks like a golf club but is a learner (L). Royal Troon is a Scottish golf links, so 'In Troon' means on a GOLF COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: both phrases are emphatic ways of saying yes, certainly.

clue.text: Running against former Labour leader

parts.note: on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall
Michael Foot led the British Labour Party from 1980 to 1983

explanation.surface: A campaign is being mounted in opposition to a past head of the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot led Britain's Labour Party in the early 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a plan under way or in progress is said to be afoot, or running.

clue.text: Youngster clear about English uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue, an uprising reads the letters from bottom to top
about means the first word is placed around the abbreviation

parts.note: to net is to clear as profit

explanation.surface: A young person stays clear of an English rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside NET to give NEET, and 'uprising' turns that round to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation: a youngster aged thirteen to nineteen is a teenager, shortened colloquially.

clue.text: Cheese, a little green one, with nothing at all for wrapping

indicators.note: wrapping means the slang word goes round the alien

parts.note: FA is short for sweet FA, slang for nothing at all
ET, the film alien, is a little green extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: Describes a cheese wrapped in a bit of greenery with no other covering.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all. 'A little green one' is ET, the alien.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a crumbly Greek white cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: International ministry adding English folio in double index

indicators.note: adding says the ministry is followed by the remaining pieces

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, the British ministry handling international affairs

indicators.note: in places these two letters inside the lookalike

parts.note: a ringer is a double, as in a dead ringer

explanation.surface: A foreign office adds an English folio to a twin-volume index.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double index' looks like one phrase about a catalogue. 'in' puts EF inside RINGER, a lookalike as in a dead ringer.
explanation.definitionFit: The index finger is another name for the pointing finger next to the thumb.

clue.text: Renewal of Pilsner — the men are blotto

indicators.note: blotto is slang for very drunk, so these letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Drinkers order another round of lager because the men are already drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blotto' rearranges PILSNER and THE MEN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a renewal of supplies is a restocking, a filling up again.

clue.text: Will I get indemnified covering this musician?

indicators.note: the phrase covers the name, holding it within its letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an insurance policy will protect them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' sounds like insurance cover but means the name runs across 'wilL I GET Indemnified'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: György Ligeti was a Hungarian composer, known for music used in 2001: A Space Odyssey.

clue.text: Intense academic, old, turned on and off

parts.note: a prof is a professor, an academic

indicators.note: taking letters on and off means alternately, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A dedicated professor of a certain age keeps switching the device on and off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on and off' looks like a light switch but picks alternate letters of 'turned': tUrNeD gives UND.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a profound feeling is deep and strongly felt.

clue.text: Result of straining pro overturned in report

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the report word

parts.note: to file is to report, as journalists file a story

indicators.note: overturned means the word for pro is read backwards

parts.note: pro is short for prostitute, as is tart

explanation.surface: A report finds a professional was upset in some dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pro' looks like an expert but is a prostitute (TART); 'overturned' gives TRAT, which goes 'in' FILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical sense: the liquid that has passed through a filter is what comes out of straining.

clue.text: Approve traitor on condition that morality is finally observed

parts.note: a rat is a turncoat or traitor
if means provided that, on condition that

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word morality

explanation.surface: Someone backs a turncoat provided that ethics are respected at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to ratify a treaty or decision is to approve it formally.

clue.text: Desire full bust? — here's Iris

indicators.note: bust means broken, so these letters are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Seems to be a cheeky remark about a woman's figure called Iris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iris' looks like a woman's name but is the flower. 'bust' rearranges DESIRE and FULL.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the heraldic lily of France is a stylised iris flower.

clue.text: New direction for stopping bad reaction and rash

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so these letters go into the middle of the jumble
bad means the letters of reaction are messed up

parts.note: side can mean direction, as in which side the wind is coming from

explanation.surface: A new treatment is tried to halt an allergic reaction and skin eruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin complaint but means thoughtless. 'bad' rearranges REACTION into INCO...RATE, and NSIDE is 'stopping' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rash behaviour is hasty and thoughtless of others.

clue.text: Answer for nothing in hypothetical subject

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of the other

parts.note: notional means hypothetical or theoretical
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Sounds like advice on what to write for a theoretical topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject' looks like a topic but is a citizen. 'for' puts A where the O was in NOTIONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a subject of a state, a citizen, is one of its nationals.

clue.text: After that, avifauna regularly circulating about capital

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the picked letters surround the other word
regularly takes every other letter of avifauna, starting with the first

parts.note: then means after that

explanation.surface: Pictures birds flying round a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the odd letters of avifauna, and 'circulating' wraps them round the time word. 'about capital' is adjectival: concerning Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Relation: the adjective describes things relating to Athens, the Greek capital.

clue.text: Thoroughly investigate bishop for breaking plates in Lambeth?

indicators.note: breaking means splitting the other word open to fit inside

parts.note: plates of meat is Cockney rhyming slang for feet, and Lambeth is a Cockney part of London
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: Suggests a bishop smashing crockery at Lambeth Palace, the Archbishop of Canterbury's London home.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambeth Palace makes 'bishop' look apt, but Lambeth here means Cockney London. 'Plates' is rhyming slang for feet (plates of meat).
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to ferret out is to search persistently, as the animal hunts rabbits.

clue.text: Propulsion unit black following crash

indicators.note: following means the colour comes after the collision word

parts.note: to ram is to crash into
jet is a deep glossy black

explanation.surface: A black engine is fitted after an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a jet engine that compresses air by its forward speed, with no compressor.

clue.text: Tree god, sporting beard, on horse

indicators.note: on means the god piece follows the horse letter in an across clue

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for horse, as in heroin slang

indicators.note: sporting means wearing, so the beard and god are combined, the bristle round the deity

parts.note: an awn is the bristly beard on barley or grass
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A bearded god sits astride a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beard' is not a man's beard but the bristle on barley ears; 'sporting' has the Norse god wearing it, and 'on' puts horse first.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a thorny shrub or small tree, often used for hedges.

clue.text: Season with berry, reportedly

parts.note: berry sounds like bury, and to bury is to inter

explanation.surface: A dish is seasoned with a berry, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like a verb for spicing food but is the time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the coldest of the four seasons of the year.

clue.text: Some brass rubbings orginally pinched by grave individual

indicators.note: pinched by means held tightly inside the grave word

parts.note: a tomb is a grave

indicators.note: originally (misspelt in the clue) takes the first letter of rubbings

parts.note: one means a single individual

explanation.surface: Brass rubbings from church tombs are lifted by a solemn person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass rubbings' suggests church tomb brasses, but 'Some brass' is the definition: one brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a slide instrument from the brass section of an orchestra.

clue.text: Fight island to stop corruption

indicators.note: to stop means to plug the gap in the decay word

parts.note: rot is decay or corruption

explanation.surface: An island community battles to end corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a riot is a violent public disturbance or brawl.

clue.text: Port wine, a quarter of it, consumed by bum

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: nates is the anatomical word for buttocks

indicators.note: one of the four letters of wine, a quarter of the word, here its third

explanation.surface: Someone downs part of a glass of port with a bum sitting by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port wine' looks like one drink; 'Port' is the definition. 'consumed by' puts N inside NATES, the buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a French city on the Loire, historically a major Atlantic seaport.

clue.text: Warning man on board in crew's quarters

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
a castle, or rook, is a chess piece, a man on the board

explanation.surface: A sailor on deck shouts a warning about where the crew sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' looks like a sailor but is a chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the forward part of a ship below deck, where sailors traditionally lived.

clue.text: Seeing that limitless existence — pull the other one

parts.note: as means because, seeing that

indicators.note: limitless means the word for existence loses its first and last letters

parts.note: life is existence

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that life is endless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limitless' trims LIFE to IF.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: both are scornful expressions of disbelief, meaning I don't believe you.
